subject: Cloud Computing
title: How CDNs Transform Speed
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How CDNs Transform Speed.

hook.text: Netflix streams to 230 million users without buffering. Their secret: thousands of CDN servers worldwide.

buildup.text: CDNs cache content at edge locations around the world. Users download from the nearest server, not the origin.

discovery.text: CloudFront has 450+ edge locations. Cloudflare has 310+. Akamai has 4,100+. Speed is about geography.

twist.text: CDNs don't just cache. Modern CDNs run serverless functions, handle DDoS attacks, and terminate TLS at the edge.

climax.text: Without CDNs, every request would travel to the origin server. The internet would feel ten times slower.

punchline.text: CDNs make the internet feel fast. Distance disappears.

quiz.question: How do CDNs improve web performance?
options: By caching content at edge locations closest to users worldwide
By compressing all web pages to a single kilobyte
By routing all traffic through a single high-speed server

details.summary: CDNs cache content at hundreds of global edge locations so users receive data from the closest server. This can reduce latency from hundreds of milliseconds to single digits. CDNs also absorb traffic spikes and protect origin servers from overload.
details.whyItMatters: Page load speed directly impacts user experience and conversion rates. A CDN is the simplest infrastructure change that delivers the largest performance improvement for global audiences.
takeaways: Serves content from edge locations nearest to each user
Reduces latency from hundreds of milliseconds to single digits
Absorbs DDoS attacks and traffic spikes at the edge

faq.question: How much faster does a CDN make a website?
faq.answer: For global audiences, CDNs typically reduce page load times by 40 to 60 percent. Time to first byte can drop from 200-500 milliseconds to under 20 milliseconds. The improvement is greatest for users farthest from the origin server.

faq.question: Do CDNs work for dynamic content?
faq.answer: Yes. Modern CDNs cache API responses with short TTLs, use edge compute to generate personalized content, and optimize TCP connections to the origin. Even uncacheable requests benefit from optimized network paths between edge and origin.
